items.headline: Big tech sells off on AI spending, not AI demand
items.why: Investors are no longer rewarding capex announcements on faith and are asking to see margin improvement from AI workloads first, which turns spending plans into a downside catalyst rather than an upside one.

items.headline: Chip equipment makers outperform the chip designers
items.why: Money is rotating toward the companies selling the tools rather than the ones buying them, which is what a capacity build-out looks like before it shows up in end demand.

items.headline: Advanced packaging capacity is still the binding constraint on AI chips
items.why: The bottleneck is packaging rather than wafer supply, so extra fab capacity does not translate into more shipped accelerators until packaging catches up.

items.headline: Moderna jumps on late-stage melanoma vaccine results with Merck
items.why: A single trial readout moved a large-cap more than the whole index moved that day, a reminder that healthcare event risk is still the biggest single-name mover in this market.

items.headline: Short squeeze drives the sharpest crypto rally in weeks
items.why: Roughly $1.44bn of short positions were liquidated, meaning the move was driven by forced buying rather than new money, and squeezes of that kind fade unless spot demand follows.

items.headline: Ether, Solana and XRP outrun Bitcoin on the bounce
items.why: The higher-beta majors leading a recovery is the usual early signature of risk appetite returning, and it is also what makes the move fragile if the macro trigger reverses.

items.headline: The rally still leaves the asset class far below its 2025 peak
items.why: Total market value remains roughly 40% under the 2025 high, so this is a recovery inside a drawdown rather than a new cycle, and the year-to-date numbers stay deeply negative.

items.headline: The trigger came from the bond market, not from crypto
items.why: Digital assets rallied on a US Treasury liquidity decision, which shows the sector is currently trading as a leveraged bet on dollar liquidity rather than on anything native to it.

items.headline: US Treasury doubles buybacks of long-dated debt
items.why: Raising the cap from $2bn to at least $4bn per operation is the government stepping in to support demand at the long end, and it repriced yields, the dollar and every risk asset in a single session.

items.headline: Thirty-year yields had just hit their highest since 2007
items.why: The intervention follows long yields reaching levels not seen in nearly two decades, which frames the buyback as a response to stress rather than a routine liquidity adjustment.

items.headline: US public debt passes $40 trillion for the first time
items.why: Crossing that line while long-term borrowing costs are near two-decade highs is what makes the interest bill, rather than the debt total itself, the number that constrains policy from here.

items.headline: UAE suspends economic dealings with Iran as shipping is disrupted
items.why: Vessels turning back and a reported strike near the strait put a live risk premium under crude, independent of inventories or demand.

items.headline: Gold and silver surge as yields and the dollar drop
items.why: Both metals moved on the same Treasury announcement, confirming this leg is a real-rate and dollar story rather than a fresh safe-haven bid.

items.headline: Silver outpaces gold again on the move up
items.why: Silver's larger percentage gain is the pattern that compresses the gold-to-silver ratio, and it is why the ratio is worth watching as a gauge of how speculative the metals bid is.

items.headline: US crude inventories build by 4.4 million barrels
items.why: A sizeable build alongside distillate stocks at a one-month low points to a market that is well supplied in crude but tight in refined product, which supports refining margins more than the barrel.

items.headline: US refinery run rates reach their highest since 2019
items.why: Refiners running this hard caps how much further product cracks can widen and pulls crude out of storage, so it works against the inventory build above.

items.headline: S&P 500 snaps a three-day losing streak, closing near 7,708
items.why: The index recovered only after the bond move, so the equity bid is currently contingent on yields staying lower rather than on anything in earnings.

items.headline: Breadth carried the tape while technology lagged
items.why: Healthcare and cyclicals did the lifting on an up day for the index, and a rally that works without the largest sector is a different market than the one traded for most of this year.

items.headline: The dollar index fell to its lowest since mid-May
items.why: A roughly 0.8% single-day drop is a large move for a currency index and it is the mechanical link between the bond announcement and the strength in metals and crypto.

items.headline: One event is driving most of today's table
items.why: Gold, silver, the dollar index and the whole crypto block all moved on the same Treasury buyback decision, so treat those green numbers as one correlated bet, not four separate signals.

items.headline: Meta and Microsoft are the weak names on the list
items.why: Both are being marked down for AI spending rather than for trading results, which is why they lag the index on the 7-day and 30-day columns.

items.headline: Oil and gas names carry a shipping risk premium
items.why: Disruption near the strait supports crude and the producers listed here, and it is a headline risk that can reverse faster than the supply and demand data underneath it.
